finding.claim: POST /restore passes unauthenticated client-supplied params[:state] through Base64.decode64 into Marshal.load, enabling arbitrary object instantiation and likely RCE via a gadget chain (chain not verifiable: no Gemfile in repo); at minimum a DoS path.
finding.source: HTTP POST parameter 'state' on /restore (app.rb:5-6), supplied by any unauthenticated network client.

trace.note: Route POST /restore defined with no authentication.
params[:state] read from request; Base64.decode64 is lenient and unvalidated.
Decoded bytes passed directly to Marshal.load; no safe mode, no class allowlist, no signature/HMAC, no size limit.
state.inspect returned to client, reflecting the constructed object graph.

finding.guards_checked: None present: no authentication, no authorization, no integrity check (signature/HMAC), no type or class allowlist, no size limit, no input validation in app.rb. Repo contains no Gemfile/config/tests that could add guards.

verdict.guard_found: none. The route at app.rb:5 has no authentication, and app.rb:6 passes params[:state] through Base64.decode64 straight into Marshal.load with no class allowlist, signature/HMAC, size limit, or validation. The only other code in the repo is /import (app.rb:10-13), which uses JSON.parse and does not guard this route. No Gemfile or config exists to add a guard.
verdict.reason: The POST /restore route at app.rb:5 is reachable anonymously, and app.rb:6 runs Marshal.load on attacker-supplied base64 with no effective control, so untrusted deserialization is confirmed. The RCE-via-gadget-chain part of the claim is not verifiable here because there is no Gemfile, but the unauthenticated Marshal.load sink itself is confirmed.

finding.claim: POST /import reflects JSON object keys unescaped into a text/html response, enabling reflected XSS on the app origin via a cross-site text/plain form POST (no CORS preflight).
finding.source: Keys of the JSON object in the raw request body of POST /import (app.rb:10-11), supplied by any client including cross-site HTML forms.
finding.sink: HTTP response body rendered as text/html (Sinatra default for string return), built at app.rb:12.

trace.note: Route POST /import defined with no authentication or CSRF protection.
request.body.read passed to JSON.parse without Content-Type check; any body the parser accepts is used.
data.keys.join(',') returned unescaped as response body; Sinatra serves it as text/html.

finding.guards_checked: No HTML escaping, no Content-Type enforcement, no CSRF token or origin check. Exploit body is valid JSON produced via text/plain form encoding, e.g. field name {"":1," with value ":0} yielding {"":1,"=":0}. Requires victim to visit attacker page; impact limited while app has no cookies/sessions.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:10-12 has no auth, no Content-Type check, no CSRF or origin check, and no HTML escaping. Sinatra serves a string return as text/html by default, so the reflected keys are rendered as markup.
verdict.reason: The attacker is anonymous, and app.rb:11 parses any body with JSON.parse regardless of Content-Type, so a cross-site text/plain form can send a valid JSON object whose key contains markup, which app.rb:12 returns unescaped as text/html. Impact is limited because the app sets no cookies or sessions, but the reflected XSS on the app origin is real.
